name: Deep Purple
lede: Deep purple is a very dark, saturated violet-purple, a name from the xkcd survey for a color the books mostly call by other names.

sections.title: Deep as a color word
sections.body: The library takes this swatch from a single source, the xkcd survey, and lists *Deep Purple* beside *Very Dark Purple* as alternate names of Midnight Purple, a near twin [1]. The nearest named color is [[aubergine]], 5.4 apart in ΔE [1]. Paterson glosses *deep* applied to a color as intense in hue, and points out that in the deep blue sea the depth belongs to the sea [2].

sections.title: Deep purples in the dictionary
sections.body:
Paterson names several deep purples with histories. The damson plum gives its name to a deep purple [3]. Modena, an artificial dye from the Italian city, gave a crimson or deep purple for church and academic robes [4]. The purple of Cassius is a deep purple named after a seventeenth-century physician [5].

The oldest deep purple is the shellfish dye. Pliny described the blackness of the dye as achieved by dyers with two kinds of shellfish [6]. In Japan, according to St Clair, a deep purple called *murasaki* was a forbidden color for ordinary people, and in the 1980s Mexico allowed a Japanese company to collect sea snails for kimono dyeing [7].

sections.title: Opinion about the color
sections.body: Birren relays a passage on Confucius, who in the *Heang Tang* did not use a deep purple or a puce for the ornaments of his dress [8]. Birren's older claims are marked contested in our notes, so read this as tradition, not evidence. In alchemy, Ball says, a bright red or a deep purple in the retort was read as a sign of success [9]. Jarman lists the rock band Deep Purple among the associations of the color, along with Hendrix and Purple Haze [10].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is almost black on screen, with lightness 10, chroma 42 and hue 323 in LCH [1]. Beside [[aubergine]], the closest names are [[dark-purple]] and [[purple]], though a near twin carries the extra alternate names noted above [1]. Screen colors are approximate.

origin.first_recorded: origin undocumented; xkcd survey in the library
